results.question: Which moment should be Gimme Some Slack's face, the one you judge it by first? (1) The workshop floor: a room of over-long cords looping across the floor, piling against the walls and plugging into a power strip at each junction, then one cord cut so its live end sparks and its dead end lies limp. (2) The yard of masts: a sagging line strung over a shed to a far mast, the mast knocked down so the wire lies sparking on the ground, a hauler shocked crossing it while the colonist sent to re-string it is safe. The other follows as showcase 2. Recommended: (1), the floor cords are what makes the mod.

results.decision: Coverage gaps from coverage_verdict.json (judge rm-coverage-judge-1793952643): (1) game_statics_reset is a built capability that ships (impl present). Its only coverage is sc_statics_new_game, which is an exploration scene with no control. An exploration scene never accepts, so this capability is not accepted by any acceptance scene or leaf. The sheet's 'delegated' line still says new-game cleanup is 'checked by their own scenes'. [scenes.json coverage_rest[game_statics_reset] -> sc_statics_new_game (kind exploration); sheet.md ## delegated]; (2) Owner-change wire cutting is built: RM_MapComponent_Aerial.cs:368 is gated by AerialSettings.cutWiresOnOwnerChange, default true. It has no inventory entry, no leaf and no scene that stages an ownership change. sc_settings lists the cutWiresOnOwnerChange flip, but with no owner change staged there is nothing to observe, so the flip proves nothing. [record.json inventory (missing entry); scenes.json sc_settings start/action]; (3) The sc_no_repeat control does not rule out what it claims. Forcing two edges to the same seed reads zero whether the distance is computed on the drawn curve or on the seed. So it cannot catch the leaf's own false_pass (distance computed on seeds, not the drawn curve). A discriminating control needs, for example, distinct seeds with identical drawn curves planted, which must read zero. [scenes.json sc_no_repeat.control; tree.json cords_never_repeat / cord_shape_variation_probe false_pass]; (4) The sc_four_looks control (two runs in the same look read the same) cannot rule out its stated alternative, looks differing only by tint. A tint-only implementation passes both the positive case and this control. The 'captures told apart' expect names no instrument or judge. [scenes.json sc_four_looks.control/expect]; (5) The sc_spans control (the same capture with nothing under the span) is not a rejection or absence case. It is the positive read repeated, so it distinguishes no mechanism. The scene needs a control that fails when the span sits at building or pawn altitude. [scenes.json sc_spans.control]; (6) The sc_gravship control (the read before launch passes) is not a control: it can never fail and rules nothing out. 'With the switch off its stated behaviour holds' names no expected observable. The restore is the boilerplate scene-rect snapshot, which cannot undo a flight that moved the ship to another map or tile. [scenes.json sc_gravship.control/expect/restore]; (7) sc_tap_theft never asserts that other factions' goodwill is unchanged. A drain that hits both the victim and the wrong faction would pass, yet the leaf's red names 'costs a different faction' and an item for exactly this is open (GSS_POWER_THEFT_FIX_WRONG_VICTIM). [scenes.json sc_tap_theft.expect; tree.json tap_steals_and_costs_goodwill.red]; (8) The sc_fallen_span control (an unpowered span cut, both ends dead) tests live/dead by power. It does not rule out its stated alternative, a span hidden on cut. Its rules_out does not match its case. [scenes.json sc_fallen_span.control]; (9) floor.json says the walk establishes memory (heap and texture MB before and after) and save_size (mid-way and end). Neither the sc_walk expect nor the walk_scavenger_base oracle reads them. sc_walk also has no expect for its master off/on step or for the frame-time bar the leaf oracle names. Its restore is the scene-rect snapshot, which does not fit a week-long fresh colony on his full list. [floor.json memory/save_size; scenes.json sc_walk expect/restore; tree.json walk_scavenger_base.oracle_proposed]; (10) Fuel-puddle ignition by a live fallen wire is part of the built fallen_wire_shock capability ('can ignite fuel puddles'; its chemfuel half has passed once). No leaf or scene asserts it. sc_shock only treats a fuel puddle as an alternative to rule out. [record.json inventory fallen_wire_shock; tree.json fallen_wire_shocks_crossers; scenes.json sc_shock]; (11) His words (s_no_plug_in_pipe_slot) are 'favor diagonal approaches sliding underneath'. No leaf or scene tests the slide-under approach itself; only 'no plug in a pipe slot' is asserted, and the slideUnder switch flip in sc_settings names no observable. Separately, the inventory says WaterproofConduit draws transparent, but sc_conduit_invisible stages only a plain run, so WaterproofConduit is never shown. [record.json scope s_no_plug_in_pipe_slot, inventory invisible_conduit; tree.json drawing_true_to_grid, conduit_invisible; scenes.json sc_true_to_grid, sc_conduit_invisible, sc_settings]

(1) Its red, 'a cut leaves both ends sparking', contradicts the root ('sparking where it is live and dead where it is not'): when the far side has its own power source, both ends ARE live. Restate it so the reject is an end with no path to any power source that sparks, or a live end drawn dead. Keep the false_pass about choosing live/dead by which side is nearer the generator. (2) Sheet line 24 only states the positive case. Make it state the reject plainly ('an end cut off from all power that sparks is wrong'), so a Reader of the sheet alone rejects e10. (3) For the next exam, the control should remove a leaf that nothing else backs up (for example statics_clear_between_games or cut_live_and_dead_ends), not drawing_true_to_grid, which his words and the walk's red also cover. results.question: In the workshop-floor showcase, a cord is cut and its live end lies sparking on the floor. A hauler walks over that end on another job. Should they be shocked, as with a fallen overhead wire, and should the colonist rebuilding that cut conduit be safe, as the re-stringer is? Or is a sparking floor end only a look, harmless to touch? (1) Same rule as fallen wires: crossers shocked, the one fixing it safe. (2) Harmless: the spark is only drawn. Recommended: (1), since your words say 'the sparking end', not 'the fallen wire'.
